title: EIF quality-per-token benchmark result record
description: One record = one attempt at (task, mode). The harness emits one of these per attempt - success, task failure, harness error, timeout, or abort - never omitted, never overwritten. A restarted attempt is a NEW record linked to the one it restarts via attempt_id/parent_attempt_id/attempt_kind, not a count folded into the record that preceded it - so the full retry history survives in the raw record stream, not just a tally. See docs/benchmarks/README.md for the corpus, modes, and methodology this schema serves. Validated with jsonschema's Draft202012Validator, same convention as every other EIF schema.

attempt_id.description: Unique id for this specific attempt - never reused, including across a restart of the same (task_id, mode, run_index).

parent_attempt_id.description: The attempt_id this one restarts, if any. null for the first attempt at a given (task_id, mode, run_index). Following parent_attempt_id backward reconstructs the full retry chain - the raw record stream is append-only, so that chain is never lost the way a bare counter would lose it.

attempt_kind.description: Why this attempt exists. 'initial' has parent_attempt_id: null; every 'retry_*' value requires a non-null parent_attempt_id (cross-checked, not just documented - see eif_benchmark.py's validate-result).

task_id.description: References a task in the corpus (see docs/benchmarks/fixtures/).

mode.description: A: no EIF, no Graphify, no RTK. B: EIF (eifctl), no Graphify, no RTK. C: EIF plus consumed-and-recorded healthy/fresh Graphify evidence. D: mode C plus healthy RTK and attempt-attributed content-free telemetry.

run_index.description: 0-based repeat index for this exact (task_id, mode) pair - repeated runs are required by methodology, not optional. Distinct from attempt lineage: run_index identifies WHICH of the planned repeats this is; attempt_id/parent_attempt_id identify whether THIS run_index needed a restart.

randomized_order_seed.description: Seed used to randomize mode order for this run batch, so mode order itself is not a confound. null only for a single manual/debug run, never for a real batch.

settings.description: Free-form: temperature, max_tokens, thinking/reasoning effort, etc. - whatever this run's harness actually configured, so a later reader can tell if two records are truly comparable.

tool_versions.description: Pinned versions of any tooling this run's mode depended on (e.g. eifctl for mode B) - required so mixed tool versions are never silently compared as equivalent. Absent only for mode A, which depends on none.

eifctl.description: Read directly from the materialized instance's own .eif/framework.lock.yaml (package section) - never re-derived from a separate `eifctl version` call or PATH lookup, which could silently resolve to a DIFFERENT install than the one that actually materialized this attempt.

environment.description: The execution environment this attempt actually ran in - a mode's behavior/cost is not assumed portable across operating systems without evidence.

target_ref.description: For synthetic_fixture: the fixture's own id/path in the corpus. For public_repository: 'owner/name'.

adapter.description: The eifctl adapter this mode's instance was configured for (e.g. 'claude-code') - null for mode A, which has no adapter/governance at all.

frozen_commit_sha.description: Required for public_repository (reproducibility); a synthetic fixture instead pins a fixture-bundle digest in provenance.source_digest.

provenance.description: How this exact input state was materialized for this run.

source_digest.description: Combined sha256 of the fixture's immutable source tree at materialize time - lets validate-result confirm the attempt actually ran against the fixture it claims to, not a hand-edited or drifted copy.

completion_success.description: Did the run reach a terminal state the harness recognizes as 'done', regardless of whether the result was CORRECT - see tests_passed for correctness.

mutation_check_passed.description: Anti-cheating signal: did reverting the produced fix (applying the fixture's known mutation) make tests_passed drop as expected? false or null is itself a finding (the test suite may not actually exercise the fix) - never silently omitted from aggregation.

factual_errors.description: Count of claims made during the run that were checked and found false.

review_findings.description: Count of code-review-style findings against the produced change.

rework_loops.description: Count of times the run had to backtrack/redo prior work within the same attempt.

setup_cost_seconds.description: One-time cost to prepare the environment for this mode (e.g. installing eifctl), amortized or recorded per run per methodology.

index_or_graph_refresh_cost_seconds.description: Cost to (re)build the knowledge index (mode B+) or the structural graph (mode C+) for this input state - null for mode A.

maintenance_overhead_notes.description: Free text: anything about keeping the mode's tooling current/working that a raw number doesn't capture.

measurement.description: Provenance of metrics.input_tokens/output_tokens/tool_calls - an agent-runner's own self-reported JSON is not trusted as measured truth without labeling where it came from (adoption-hardening round). Required on every non-blocked-mode record; see eif_benchmark.py's aggregate, which refuses to silently blend records with different `source` or different `exact` values into one group, and refuses to publish a group containing any record missing this field entirely.

source.description: fake-runner: this round's only agent-runner, deterministic and free - never a stand-in for real quality-per-token evidence. provider-usage: token counts read from the model provider's own usage/billing API. client-telemetry: counted client-side by the agent harness itself. estimated: approximated (e.g. a tokenizer estimate), not authoritative.

exact.description: true only for provider-usage/client-telemetry readings taken directly from an authoritative counter; false for any estimate. fake-runner records are exact (the fake values are exactly what was reported), but that exactness says nothing about real-agent cost - see source.

collector_version.description: Version of whatever collected this measurement (e.g. the fake-runner script's own version, or a telemetry library version) - null if not applicable/unknown.

integration_evidence.description: Privacy-safe evidence for integrations actually consumed by this attempt. Required for C/D and forbidden for A/B. It stores provider states, versions, digests, capability names and counters only.

status.description: success/partial/failure: the agent reached a terminal state, judged by test/review outcome. harness_error: the harness itself broke (not the agent's fault). timeout: the wall-time/tool budget was exceeded. aborted: stopped deliberately (e.g. operator-cancelled) before a terminal state.

raw_log_ref.description: Pointer (path or URL) to the full raw transcript/log for this run - the record itself stays a compact summary, never the full transcript inline. Any transcript this points at must pass a privacy scan before publication (see D-12).
